land.text: Berbice, merged on 21 July 1831 with Demerara-Essequibo into British Guiana

successors.note: British since September 1803 'for good'; ceded by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814, ratified by the Netherlands on 20 November 1815.

capitals.name: New Amsterdam (Berbice)
capitals.note: The page: 'Fort Nassau was the capital until 1785 according to the infobox' (the body text says 1790); New Amsterdam grew around Fort Sint Andries. Fort Nassau's coordinates are not on the page, so the dot stays at New Amsterdam.

correction.text: the Berbice River settlement: 'Berbice was settled in 1627 by the businessman Abraham van Peere' from Vlissingen

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first eastern Guyana cells are in 1629.

correction.text: the 35 Cliopatria cells east of 57.9 W (the Berbice and Canje rivers), from the New Netherland row's wrong 1629 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area; 'The colony lay along the Berbice River' with the Canje meeting Fort Sint Andries.

correction.text: 34 cells, one fewer than 1629, to the British cession

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The 1763-64 slave rising under Coffy and the occupations alternate in the ledger; Cliopatria has no Guyana cell in 1781-1787 and 1797-1799.

ledger.note: 1627: Abraham van Peere settles Berbice under the West India Company's suzerainty ('Berbice was settled in 1627 by the businessman Abraham van Peere').
1678: a charter makes Berbice 'a hereditary fief of the Dutch West India Company, in the possession of the Van Peere family'.
1712 (November): 'Berbice was briefly occupied by the French' under Jacques Cassard.

1714 (24 October): Van Peere's relatives and associates paid the ransom 'thereby acquiring the colony'; the French leave. The page does not say when the French withdrew, only that the ransom was paid on this date.
1720 (24 October): five owners found the Society of Berbice, a public company on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange (infobox: 24 October 1720 to 1821).
1781 (27 February): 'British forces occupied Berbice' in the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.
1782 (January): 'the colonies were recaptured by the French' (infobox: 22 January 1782).
1782 (January): the French hold Berbice until the Treaty of Paris.
1783: 'The Treaty of Paris (1783) restored Dutch rule.'
1792 (1 January): Berbice becomes a Dutch state colony.
1796 (22 April): 'The colony was on 22 April 1796 again captured by Britain, however this time without a fight.'
1802 (27 March): 'until 27 March 1802, when Berbice was restored to the Batavian Republic' under the Treaty of Amiens.
1803 (September): 'the British occupied the territory again, this time for good.'
1814: the occupation becomes cession. Under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 the colony was 'formally ceded to the United Kingdom'.

1814: under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 the colony was 'formally ceded to the United Kingdom'; the Netherlands ratified it on 20 November 1815. On 21 July 1831 the British merged Berbice with Demerara-Essequibo to form British Guiana.

wars.name: Berbice slave uprising
wars.outcome: The rising began 'under the leadership of Coffy in February 1763' and continued into 1764; the rebels 'captured the south of the colony' while the outnumbered whites held the north, until Governor van Hoogenheim, with troops from neighbouring colonies and the Netherlands, suppressed it 'until well into 1764'.
wars.note: [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: the earlier note said the page is silent on land held; the Berbice page says the rebels 'captured the south of the colony'. Zones and the contest_start/contest_end pair (February 1763 to 1764, the upper Berbice River) are still to be added; listed for the gap-filler.]

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War and French Revolutionary Wars in Berbice
wars.outcome: British occupation from 27 February 1781, the French from January 1782 to the 1783 Treaty of Paris, British again from 22 April 1796 to 27 March 1802, and permanently from September 1803.
wars.note: Descriptive name; the page names the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War for 1781.

certainty.note: A river colony on the Berbice and Canje; the page gives no frontier or area, and the boundary with Essequibo-Demerara is not on it.

sources.title: Berbice
sources.note: Van Peere 1627, the 1678 charter, French 1712-1714, the Society 1720, 1763 rising, occupations 1781-1783 and 1796-1814, the 1814 cession, British Guiana 1831.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. Berbice's cells (35 in 1629-1669, 34 from 1670) sit inside the New Netherland row east of 57.9 W; Essequibo and Demerara are the essequibo dossier. The 1665 English attack on Berbice was 'repelled', so no occupation is recorded. Demerara's own colony history is not covered. Written by am-06-c as a direct counterpart of the New Netherland row.
